messages:
mari: Quick Q re: prompt/prefix cache contract — I noticed two ambiguities that could break clients. 1) Should the cache key include model+variant (e.g., `gptx-8k`)? 2) What's the canonical cache hit indicator header? I saw `X-Redwood-Cache: HIT` in some responses and `x-cache-hit: 1` elsewhere. Pls confirm before I change the SDK.

jonathan: Good catch. Short answers: include model+variant in the key, yes — we need deterministic behavior when we route to compatible variants. For header, we agreed on `x-rw-cache: HIT` (lowercase header name to avoid conflicting proxies). I'll paste the contract snippet in a follow-up.

tay: Related: how do we treat streaming responses? If we stream tokens, we shouldn't advertise a hit until the full response is known. So either: a) emit `x-rw-cache: MISS` early and update logs once complete, or b) only set `x-rw-cache` on the final response (non-streamed metadata). Which do we prefer?

devon: We discussed this in design sync — prefer option (b). Set header only in the final metadata frame for streaming. For sync responses set it on the response headers. Also: we should add `cache-scope` semantics (global|customer|session) to the contract so clients can decide whether to respect shared results. Privacy reasons for customer-scoped hits.

mari: Nice. For cache key canonicalization, propose this format: `sha256(namespace||model||quant||promptPrefix||promptHash||userScopeTag)` where `namespace` is the service route, `quant` is quantization profile. Example: 
```
key = sha256("/v1/generate" + "|gptx-8k-qat" + "|prefix:Hello world" + "|u:customer-1234")
```
Is that too heavy?

jonathan: Looks good. Two notes: 1) we should canonicalize whitespace/newlines in prefix before hashing. 2) Don't include raw user ids in the key — use stable customer id or hashed id.

devon: +1. Also add `x-rw-cache-key-id` header with a short identifier (first 8 chars of sha) for debugging/tracing. Clients can ignore it but ops can map hits without leaking full keys.

tay: For backward compatibility: if a client omits `cache-scope` on requests, we should default to `customer` for now, and log a deprecation warning to encourage explicitness. We'll keep a fallback mapping for 6 months.

mari: Implementation plan: I'll submit a small schema change PR to the API contract and SDK (types + header parsing). Can someone from infra review? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-contract/pull/412 (WIP).

jonathan: Pinged. I'll review tomorrow. Quick checklist for PR: update docs/examples, add a short integration test that asserts header present on sync responses, asserts header appears only in final metadata for streams, and include a migration note.

devon: For invalidation — we need an explicit invalidation endpoint `POST /cache/invalidate` that accepts a key pattern and scope. It should return partial success and an invalidation-id. We'll wire that into the Console so teams can trigger from the UI.

mari: Sounds good. Cache invalidation payload example in PR: 
```json
{ "scope": "customer", "patterns": ["/v1/generate|gptx-*-*|prefix:ORDER_CONFIRMATION*" ] }
```
Response: `{ "invalidation_id": "inv_9a1b2c", "status": "queued" }`

tay: Small UX ask: expose `cache-hit-rate` per route and per model in Console telemetry. Ops need it for rollout decisions.

cache-bot: deployment scheduled: contract-service v2.7.1 -> staging at 2026-03-18T09:30:00Z :gear: (will run integration tests after deploy)

deploy-bot: integration tests passed for staging. smoke: generate/stream + invalidate flow OK.

jonathan: Thanks. mari — once your PR is ready, tag `@eng-platform` and we'll do a canary. If tests are green I'm OK with merging.

mari: Will do. Thanks all! :pray:

devon: FYI leaving a short note in #docs to call out the header naming and `cache-scope` default.

tay: LGTM from me. :thumbsup:
